title: When should I start a new paragraph?
examples: When do I start a new paragraph?
How long should a paragraph be?

explain.say: Imagine a whole story with no breaks, one giant block of words. Your eyes would get lost! Paragraphs are little rooms that split writing into chunks. Look at the board: a word to help you remember when to start one, TiPToP. The first chunk, Ti, stands for time.

draw.text: When should I start a new paragraph?

explain.say: Ti for time: when the time changes, start a new paragraph. The next morning, Kemi woke early. See how the time jumped? Can you think of another time jump, like later that day?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What changed? Start a new paragraph!

explain.say: Look at the second group on the board: place. When the story moves somewhere new, like At the beach, start a new paragraph. In a report, look at the third group, topic: a new idea gets a new paragraph.

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What changed? Start a new paragraph!

explain.say: The last group is person: when a new character comes in, or a new person speaks, start a new paragraph. Meanwhile, Sam was hiding. Can you see why this helps the reader?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What changed? Start a new paragraph!

explain.say: You have got it! Look back at the word on the board: Time, Place, Topic, Person. TiPToP. In handwriting, show a new paragraph by starting a new line a little way in. Challenge: in a book near you, find a paragraph break and say which TiPToP reason it is.

faq.q: When do I start a new paragraph?
faq.a: Start a new paragraph when the time, place, topic or person changes. Remember it as TiPToP.
TiPToP stands for Time, Place, Topic, Person: the four changes that tell you to begin a new paragraph.

faq.q: How long should a paragraph be?
faq.a: There is no fixed length. In school writing most paragraphs are three to six sentences, all about one main idea.
asks: How many sentences in a paragraph?

faq.q: How do I show a new paragraph?
faq.a: In handwriting, start on a new line and indent, which means leave a small gap at the start. On a computer, you can leave a blank line instead.
A topic sentence is the first sentence of a paragraph that tells the reader what the paragraph is about.

facts: The word paragraph comes from Greek, meaning written beside, from a mark once drawn in the margin.
The pilcrow, ¶, is an old symbol that marks a new paragraph.
